title: decision rights evidence board
question: Who may direct, analyze, operate, assure, and accept an urgent acquisition exception, and what evidence crosses each role boundary?
scenario: Acquisition integration: An acquired company must connect to corporate systems before a financial close.
focalRelation: Mission and appetite constrain analysis; analysis informs but does not own acceptance; the authorized business owner decides; operators implement; independent assurance and oversight receive evidence and trigger reassessment.

nodes.label: Acquisition deadline and purpose
nodes.detail: The acquisition deadline and business purpose define what the integration must achieve without replacing security accountability.

nodes.label: Risk Appetite
nodes.detail: The approved appetite sets the maximum integration risk that delegated owners may accept.

nodes.label: Authorized Owner
nodes.detail: A business owner with sufficient delegation chooses treatment, resources, and any residual-risk acceptance.

nodes.label: Security Analysis
nodes.detail: Security staff document exposure, control evidence, uncertainty, and options for the accountable owner; they do not accept business risk on the owner’s behalf.

nodes.label: Management Operation
nodes.detail: Named operators implement the approved treatment and retain evidence that the controls are working in the acquired environment.

nodes.label: Assurance
nodes.detail: Independent review reports control performance, exceptions, and residual risk back to governance.

options.label: The CISO alone owns every cyber risk
options.feedback: Security informs and operates controls, but accountable business leadership owns decisions within delegated authority.

options.label: Require documented analysis and acceptance by an authorized business owner
options.feedback: Correct. The decision needs documented risk analysis and an authorized business owner, not unilateral technical approval.

options.feedback: That shortcut ignores the decisive changed fact. The decision needs documented risk analysis and an authorized business owner, not unilateral technical approval.

assumptions: Only entities and claims anchored in the canonical unit or explicitly labeled hypothetical scenario are used.
A highlighted path means the learner is inspecting that path; it does not assert the event occurred.
The current source is authoritative for facts; this treatment reorganizes presentation without changing canonical content.
The lesson teaches one bounded decision and does not claim to exhaust every jurisdiction, vendor implementation, architecture, attack, or exception.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The ledger preserves mission and appetite constraints, separation of analysis from business acceptance, treatment ownership, operating evidence, and independent assurance. It stages those decision rights in one acquisition case; control-framework selection and a separate scope inset remain reference content rather than distinct visual controls.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Analysis informs a risk decision but does not grant authority to accept it. An authorized business owner decides within delegated appetite and escalates beyond that limit.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A role-and-evidence visual can show decision, analysis, operation, and assurance boundaries simultaneously; the current one-edge view adds less than the full accountability system requires.
